handoff: Blocking: AC4/D4 hook-file selection has no S1 test (unit without live run read within limits.stalled, skipped after; no other units' hook lines in the AC4 setup). Minor: unrecorded parity changes (story unit no longer gets slice facts via cwd prefix), utimes between appends can drop the day line or move mtime backwards, duplication. AC1-3, AC5, AC6 met; snapshots/golden unchanged; typecheck green; suite green bar a load-timeout flake in check-run.test.ts (passes alone).

findings.title: AC4 / D4 selection of hook files is untested
findings.detail:
AC4: 'Given a live run on gh-9 and hook lines for other units in the day files, when a tick runs, then it reads gh-9's hook file (and the hook files of units changed within `limits.stalled`), the trace-read observer sees no day file opened…'. The test only asserts that the tick opens no day file. Its setup has no other unit's hook lines. Nothing at S1, and nothing at any seam, shows (a) that the tick's facts carry gh-9's hook facts from its hook file, (b) that a unit with no live run whose hook file was written within limits.stalled is read, or (c) that one written before the window is skipped. That rule is packages/store/src/local-facts.ts:123-128. The store test checks unitHooksChangedAt only with toBeNumber() (packages/store/test/config-trace.test.ts:224), never against the fact's `at`.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add an S1 test that uses the fake clock. Give gh-9 a live run and give a second unit hook facts (in the hook file and the day file) but no live run. Tick inside the stalled window, then advance past it and tick again. Assert the observed facts each time (the second unit's hooks present, then empty, with gh-9's always present) and that no day file is opened.

findings.title: Hook routing parity changed without being recorded
findings.detail:
D4 says '…so decide sees the same facts', and the risk section says the facts 'must keep exactly the facts observe saw'. The old hookOfUnit matched `fact.cwd.startsWith(unit.worktree)` with no trailing '/', so the story unit (worktree `…/gh-107-slug`) also collected facts fired in its slice worktrees (`…/gh-107-slug--04-…`). It no longer does (the store test notes it at config-trace.test.ts:214). Also, a unit outside the D4 set now gets hooks: [] where it used to get facts back to the oldest live run, and the view reads lu.hooks (packages/view/src/load.ts:323). Both look like intended or harmless changes, and the snapshots and golden are unchanged, but neither is in handoff Progress as a decision.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Record both as decisions in handoff.md Progress so the person sees them at the gate.

findings.title: A throw from utimesSync drops the day-file line; mtime can move backwards
findings.detail:
utimesSync runs between the two appends. If it throws (an invalid fact.at, EPERM), the unit line is written, the day line is not, and hook.ts:153 swallows the error. Separately, a hook whose `at` is older than the last line written (two hooks racing, or 05's backfill) sets the mtime backwards. unitHooksChangedAt's doc ('the time of its last appended fact') is then wrong, and a unit can drop out of the tick's set.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Append the day line before setting the times (or catch around utimes). Only set the mtime when fact.at is later than the current mtime.

findings.title: AC1 test fires PreToolUse rather than PostToolUse
findings.detail:
AC1 names a `PostToolUse` hook, but the test fires PreToolUse. The routing is the same, so this is a nit.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optional: fire PostToolUse in the AC1 assertion.

findings.title: Duplicated code
findings.detail:
Four places repeat code that already exists. unitHookLines' parse loop repeats hookLines (trace.ts:342-348). appendHookTrace repeats appendTrace's line building (trace.ts:49-51). liveRun || unknownLaunch is computed twice (local-facts.ts:110-111, 125). openedDays repeats the inline `opened` helper in agent-protocol.test.ts:232-236.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Share a line parser and a line builder, and reuse one observer helper in the test.
